content: The classification of cetaceans includes various genera and species, each with distinct characteristics and taxonomic considerations. Below is a detailed description of the species and their classifications: 1. Genus Tursiops: The Indian Ocean Bottlenose Dolphin (Tursiops aduncus) and the Common Bottlenose Dolphin (Tursiops truncatus) are recognized under this genus. Both Rice and MSW3 tentatively agree on this classification, but further details can be found in species-specific articles. 2. Genus Cephalorhynchus: Commerson's Dolphin (Cephalorhynchus commersonii), Chilean Dolphin (Cephalorhynchus eutropia), Heaviside's Dolphin (Cephalorhynchus heavisidii), and Hector's Dolphin (Cephalorhynchus hectori) are included in this genus. 3. Genus Delphinus: The Long-beaked Common Dolphin (Delphinus capensis), Short-beaked Common Dolphin (Delphinus delphis), and Arabian Common Dolphin (Delphinus tropicalis) are classified here. Rice recognizes Delphinus tropicalis as a separate species, while MSW3 does not. 4. Genus Feresa: The Pygmy Killer Whale (Feresa attenuata) is the sole species in this genus. 5. Genus Globicephala: This genus includes the Short-finned Pilot Whale (Globicephala macrorhynchus) and the Long-finned Pilot Whale (Globicephala melas). 6. Genus Grampus: The Risso's Dolphin (Grampus griseus) is the only species in this genus. 7. Genus Lagenodelphis: The Fraser's Dolphin (Lagenodelphis hosei) is the sole representative of this genus. 8. Genus Lagenorhynchus: This genus includes the Atlantic White-sided Dolphin (Lagenorhynchus acutus), White-beaked Dolphin (Lagenorhynchus albirostris), Peale's Dolphin (Lagenorhynchus australis), Hourglass Dolphin (Lagenorhynchus cruciger), Pacific White-sided Dolphin (Lagenorhynchus obliquidens), and Dusky Dolphin (Lagenorhynchus obscurus). 9. Genus Lissodelphis: The Northern Right Whale Dolphin (Lissodelphis borealis) and the Southern Right Whale Dolphin (Lissodelphis peronii) are included in this genus. 10. Genus Orcaella: The Irrawaddy Dolphin (Orcaella brevirostris) and the Australian Snubfin Dolphin (Orcaella heinsohni) are part of this genus. The latter was discovered in 2005 and is not yet recognized by Rice or MSW3, pending further revision. 11. Genus Orcinus: The Killer Whale (Orcinus orca) is the only species in this genus. 12. Genus Peponocephala: The Melon-headed Whale (Peponocephala electra) is the sole species in this genus. 13. Genus Pseudorca: The False Killer Whale (Pseudorca crassidens) is the only species in this genus. 14. Genus Sotalia: The Tucuxi (Sotalia fluviatilis) is classified here, but further discussion on its taxonomy can be found in species-specific articles. 15. Genus Sousa: This genus includes the Pacific Humpback Dolphin (Sousa chinensis), Indian Humpback Dolphin (Sousa plumbea), and Atlantic Humpback Dolphin (Sousa teuszii). 16. Genus Stenella: The Pantropical Spotted Dolphin (Stenella attenuata), Clymene Dolphin (Stenella clymene), Striped Dolphin (Stenella coeruleoalba), Atlantic Spotted Dolphin (Stenella frontalis), and Spinner Dolphin (Stenella longirostris) are included in this genus. 17. Genus Steno: The Rough-toothed Dolphin (Steno bredanensis) is the only species in this genus. 18. Family Monodontidae: Genus Delphinapterus: The Beluga (Delphinapterus leucas). Genus Monodon: The Narwhal (Monodon monoceros). 19. Family Phocoenidae (Porpoises): Genus Neophocaena: The Finless Porpoise (Neophocaena phocaenoides). Genus Phocoena: The Spectacled Porpoise (Phocoena dioptrica), Harbour Porpoise (Phocoena phocoena), Vaquita (Phocoena sinus), and Burmeister's Porpoise (Phocoena spinipinnis). Genus Phocoenoides: The Dall's Porpoise (Phocoenoides dalli). 20. Family Physeteridae (Sperm Whales): Genus Physeter: The Sperm Whale (Physeter catodon, synonym P. macrocephalus). 21. Family Kogiidae: Genus Kogia: The Pygmy Sperm Whale (Kogia breviceps) and the Dwarf Sperm Whale (Kogia sima). MSW3 treats this genus as part of the Physeteridae family. 22. Superfamily Platanistoidea (River Dolphins): Family Iniidae: Genus Inia: The Amazon River Dolphin (Inia geoffrensis). Family Lipotidae: Genus Lipotes: The extinct Baiji (Lipotes vexillifer). MSW3 treats this genus as part of Iniidae. Family Pontoporiidae: Genus Pontoporia: The Franciscana (Pontoporia blainvillei). MSW3 treats this genus as part of Iniidae. Family Platanistidae: Genus Platanista: The Ganges and Indus River Dolphin (Platanista gangetica). MSW3 treats Platanista minor as a separate species, with the common names Ganges River Dolphin and Indus River Dolphin, respectively. This detailed taxonomy reflects the diversity and complexity of cetacean classification, with ongoing debates and revisions in the scientific community.
